name: Trivikrama Perumal Temple, Sirkazhi
deity: Vishnu as Trivikrama (Thadalan) Perumal, with the Goddess Lokanayaki
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: In Sirkazhi, Vishnu stands as Trivikrama, the Thadalan whose raised foot spans the worlds — the Divya Desam of Kazhicheerama Vinnagaram, sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: The Trivikrama temple of Sirkazhi, also called Thadalan Koil and known in the hymns as Thirukkazhicheerama Vinnagaram, is one of the 108 Divya Desams — the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham — in Chola Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar offered its mangalasasanam in the Periya Thirumozhi. An older name of the place is Patalikavanam. The presiding lord is Trivikrama, the Thadalan, with the Goddess Lokanayaki, and the temple is today administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. No inscriptions or dated history for the shrine are recorded in the sources consulted.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan of the Chola country. Its sanctum is crowned by the vimana known as Pushkalavartha, and the lord is worshipped in the posture of Trivikrama, Vamana grown to measure the worlds, with one foot raised. The temple has two sacred waters: the Shankha Pushkarini and the Chakra Theertham, named for the conch and the discus of Vishnu.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Romasa, whose body-hairs are said to be tied to the span of Brahma's life, and who asked Vishnu to remain here as Trivikrama. Tradition also remembers a meeting in Sirkazhi between Thirumangai Alvar and the Shaiva saint Sambandar: after the Alvar sang his hymn, Sambandar is said to have honoured him with a vel, a spear.
sections.festivals: The Brahmotsavam, the great annual festival, is held in the month of Vaikasi (May–June). Vaikunta Ekadashi and the days of the Alvars follow the Vaishnava calendar. Confirm dates locally. The temple is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, and local priests can confirm the festival calendar.
sections.experience: Stand before Trivikrama and look for the raised foot that gives the lord his name. Sirkazhi is also a town of famous Shaiva shrines, and the Alvar's meeting with Sambandar makes this a fitting place to reflect on the shared devotion of the Kaveri country. The temple pairs well with Thiruvali-Thirunagari and the Thirunangur group nearby.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Sirkazhi town, Mayiladuthurai district, reached by road and by the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai rail line, on which Sirkazhi is a station. The nearest major airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away.
